patterns.what_worked: Targeted greps + small sed reads kept a 334 KB practice_ui.lua and six 160-310 KB class files out of context; a single provider contract replaced four hardcoded routes; the fixture-provider pattern let the existing suites keep their behavioural coverage; mutation proofs on a /tmp copy proved every new guard.
patterns.what_was_hard: The carry-over from the aborted attempt: the resume brief said no code had changed but the edits were on disk, so disk state had to be re-verified before doing anything. The 2-warning luacheck floor also forced two fixture-local cleanups (unused helper, shadowed name).
patterns.skill_gap: The error-path wording generalisation (per-class refusal strings -> generic) is a user-visible change that should have been decided with the orchestrator up front rather than noted after the fact.

escalation.recommendation: Orchestrator review + operator in-client check: Auto and an explicit non-playing pick on each class, a Start/Stop Fight round-trip per drill, and design mode showing the paladin's seal/success elements only with PALADIN active.
